Frequently Asked Questions (AAC) This page answers common questions for **ArcheAge Classic (AAC)** players. Note: AAC is based on the classic **3.5-era** ArcheAge with custom changes. See: Getting Started and Custom Server Changes. Server basics What are the server rates? Commonly referenced rates: **XP x2**, **Vocation x2**, **Honor (PvP) x4**, **Honor (PvE/Quests) x2**. Do I need Patron? No. AAC has **free Patron benefits for all players**. How does Labor work? Labor regenerates **online and offline**. Commonly referenced values: **40 labor / 5 minutes**, max **10,000**. Leveling / early progression What’s the fastest way to level? Follow **green story quests**. Most players skip/ignore most **yellow quests** unless they specifically need them. What is a Growthstone? An **EXP consumable**. Use it directly from your inventory. Catch-up gear / gearing When do I get catch-up gear? At **level 50**, you receive a **Catch-up Gear Box**. What should I do right after I open the catch-up box? Don’t stress perfect min/max immediately. Early PvP survivability gems people commonly recommend: **Toughness (pants)** + **Resilience (chest)**. Use Activity Tokens to start the upgrade quest at a **Daru Auctioneer** (Mirage portal area), then use the **Soulforged anvil (Diamond Shores)**. Is it better to regrade myself or buy finished pieces? Often, buying a finished piece is cheaper than eating RNG. Dungeon gear is generally an easier regrade target than some crafted/obsidian paths. Emerald / Hasla weapons (AAC) What are Emerald weapons? A custom starter weapon line. Upgrading is **safe (synthesis)**, not regrade RNG. How do I get an Emerald weapon? Bring a **normal Emerald**. Go to Hasla → **Tehmi Ruins / Abandoned Drill Camp**. Talk to **Fragment Researcher Soa** → trade Emerald for **Infused Emerald**. Use the bench behind Soa to craft the weapon. For upgrading Emerald (Hasla) weapons, does the fodder weapon have to match weapon type? **No.** It does not have to be the same weapon type. Activity Tokens What are Activity Tokens? A server-specific progression currency used mainly on **Mirage Isle**. Where do I get token quests? Most are picked up from **Shadow Daru** in each main capital. What are common token sources? Weekly quests (Fri/Sat/Sun resets) + daily merit-style token quest. See Activity Tokens. Trade packs / charcoal How do I get Charcoal Stabilizer? Deliver a **trade pack cross-continent** to a **Resource Trader** (West-made packs turned in East, or vice-versa). Common examples players mention: **Solis / Villanelle / Ynystere**. Housing / land Where do I get the free 8x8 + 16x16 farm? From the **Blue Salt Brotherhood land questline**. Video guide: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PBCb4NqijDA I turned in the pack but can’t find the next 16x16 quest NPC. **WEST:** talk to **Misty** on the Crescent Throne docks (Solzreed). **EAST:** talk to **Jasmine** on the Austera docks (Solis). Fishing Do I need lures for ocean sportfishing? Depends on your **rod**. When you try sportfishing it should tell you "Not enough X lure". Where do I buy lures? Fishing boats have a small **fish bucket** you can interact with to buy lures. What’s the difference between Lures and Chum? **Lures** are used **per cast**. **Chum** is **Chopped Fish Bucket** used to **activate a fishing pool**. Common issues / troubleshooting My settings reset every time I close the game. Try: go to **Character Select** before exiting. If it still happens, rename `Documents\\AAClassic` to `AAClassicOLD` to force the client to recreate settings. Settings reset after a crash. After changing UI/settings: press **Exit Game**, then click **Cancel** — this forces settings to save even if you later crash. Camera bug camera stuck and you can only move forward with mouse. Try switching **Camera Style** between **Action / Classic**. Is the server up / maintenance? Check: https://status.aa-classic.com/status/main Payments / coins PayPal/card payment fails — another way? Website **Donate** tab → **Alternative Payment Methods** → **PlayCardExpress** (PayPal & Gameflip). Guilds / social Is there a French guild? Check **#guild-recruitment** in Discord. Reporting bugs If something seems broken, include: - your **level + faction + location** - what you tried - screenshot/error text If it’s account/entitlement-related or you’re hard-stuck, open a support ticket:https://aa-classic.com/profile?tab=support

Adventurer's guide is new customly added tab in game. The Guide has Paths that are missions that need to be done in order to proceed to the next grade of missions. The mission are to help hew players navigate the game and see what kinda things are important at the get go. A New Adventure Grand REWARDS Ancestral Warrior Medal (x5) Activity Tokens (x50) Epherium Cloak Kit Sealed Epherium Cloak Unique Auroran Synthesis Sotne (x4) Warrior Medals (x50) Achieve Lv50 Get to lvl 50 by doing green quests and by using Adventurers Growthstones. > Hamiltons Guide for New Players United We Stand Make a new guild or join an existing guild. Pressing default key SHIFT + V opens the Community tab and under it is guild tab. Pick a guild that suits your playstyle or make your on by talking to the Guild Manager. Reach 4000 Gearscore Get your gearscore to 4000 or more. After getting to lvl 50 the achievement rewards the player with the catch up set called Soulforged Armor and Hellkissed Weapons and equipping these should bring the player to 4k gearscore. Vocation Knowledge Reach 10,000 proficiency on any profession. Proficiencies are harvesting and crafting actions in the game. Can be found under Skills > usually K keybind. Till Its Like It Is Do enough Blue Salt Brotherhood quests to obtain Scarecrow Design. Guide for the questline here > Hamiltons Guide for Blue Salt Brotherhood Guestline (both nations in same video!) Gotta Catch Em All Buy a Battle Pet. Battle Pets are animals or creatures that players can use to attack enemies to help with dps or combat in general. They can wear gear to better their stats. (Pokemon fights, lol.) Battle Pets can be obtained from different places but the easiest being pet stand that sell each pet for 10 silver. Two easy battle pets mentioned here are Cats and Wolfhounds. They both cost 10 silver per pet. Cat pet Wolfhound Pet Rare REWARDS Ancestral Warrior Medal (x5) Activity Tokens (x25) Honor Points (x10 000) Warrior Medals (x50) Scroll: Seaskimmer Speedboat (15d) Achieve Lv55 Keep leveling up with the quests and Adventurer Growthstones. After those are done start going to the daily events to gain experience. Guides for bosses in Guides tab of the Adventurers Guide. United We Stand Make a new family or join existing one. When creating a family and adding a member to the family players must buy Family Certificate from any General Merchant. Family tab is under Community (SHIFT +V) by default. Hounded to Death Kill Hound of Kyrios. Join a CR raid in the nation chat and complete this task by killing one of the big bosses that spawns after the mobs are dead. Vocation Knowledge 2 Reach 40,000 proficiency on any profession. Crop Whisperer Build a Scarecrow Farm. Follow Hamiltons guide in order to get both designs 8x8 and 16x16. Land for new player can be found in Swirling Meadow and occasionally other places. Into The Dungeon Complete the "Greater Bounty: Ancient Titan Musperosa" Quest. The quests can be found on task boards outside the dungeon entrance. Port to Greater Howling Abyss and defeat the last boss. The Ultimate Gliding Experience Craft an Ultimate Glider. How to Make the Basic Glider explains where to get all the designs for the crafting. Crafting happens at Carpentry Workbench. Arcane REWARDS Priceless Coin Warrior Medals (x50) Arctic Earthstone (x50) Bound Spellbook: Authority (x10) Abyssal Knowledge To access Abyssal skills for each skillset players must complete a quest related to the skillset. Guide for Abyssal Skills. Reach 4500 Gearscore Keep watching Hamiltons video linked before. There is also written guide, Gearing Guide. Vocation Knowledge 3 Reach 90,000 proficiency on any profession. Emerald Weaponsmith Obtain Hasla Emerald Weapon or Craft an Artic Earthstone. Making a Hasla Weapon do check the written guide here or IcyZinHD guide video. Just for the Arctic Earthstone players need to kill few mobs in Hasla or Karkasse, buy Faded Hasla Fragment from NPC in Hasla Abandoned Drill Camp and then craft the stone to complete the mission. A Tale of Pristine Jewelry Start Dream Ring or Ynys Ring questline. Written guide for Dream Ring questline. Written guide for Ynys Guardian Ring questline. Bigger is Better Craft a Clipper. The Clipper designs are sold in Gilda star hop for 50 gilda each. After nuying the design place the drydock in water and start building. The drydock needs variable amounts of lumber-, fabric-, and iron packs. Clipper Materials can be found in Folio (O by default) and crafted in Shipyard Workbench. Time for Work Obtain a Territory Work Permit. This can be bough from the guild shop with Prestige. Community > Guild > Prestige Shop Heroic The Dread Necromancer Kill Anthalon. Anthalon is a world boss that spawns in Sungold Fields after Auroria Crimson Rift is done. X up in the nation for x Anth to join a raid. Check more info from the Guide for Crimson Rift (Auroria). Epic Regrading Journey Regrade gearpiece to Divine once. Cloaked in Divinity Collect Divine-grade Epherium Cloak. Theres No Price For This Obtain a Priceless Coin. How to get Priceless Coins? Blessed By Tahyang Rank 1st-4th in a Mistmerrow Battle. Unique Coming soon. Celestial Coming soon. Other Paths Classic - Starfall - Guides Guides are miniguides for world events in the game. They tell the player where to go and who to talk to to start the quest in order to finish the event and get the rewards.

For example, if the prefix was 'data', and -- 'data1', 'data2', and 'data5' exist, it would return {1, 2, 5}. local function getArgNums(prefix, args) local nums = {} for k, v in pairs(args) do local num = tostring(k):match('^' .. prefix .. '([1-9]%d*)$') if num then table.insert(nums, tonumber(num)) end end table.sort(nums) return nums end --Implements {{Navpills}} from the frame function p.navpills( frame ) mArguments = require( 'Module:Arguments' ) return p._navpills( mArguments.getArgs( frame ) ) end function p._navpills( args ) if not args then return 'Missing arguments' end local html = mw.html.create( 'div' ):addClass( 'template-navpills' ):attr( 'role', 'navigation' ) for i, _ in ipairs( getArgNums( 'page', args ) ) do if not args[ 'page' .. i ] then return end local num = tostring( i ) local navpill = mw.html.create('div'):addClass('template-navpill') if args[ 'image' .. i ] then navpill:tag('div'):addClass('template-navpill-background') :wikitext( string.format( '[[File:%s|x48px|link=]]', args[ 'image' .. num ] ) ) end navpill:wikitext( string.format( '[[%s|%s]]', args[ 'page' .. num ], args[ 'text' .. num ] or args[ 'page' .. num ] ) ) html:node(navpill) end return mw.getCurrentFrame():extensionTag{ name = 'templatestyles', args = { src = 'Module:Navpills/styles.css' } } .. tostring( html ) end return p

-- This module provides easy processing of arguments passed to Scribunto from -- #invoke. It is intended for use by other Lua modules, and should not be -- called from #invoke directly. local libraryUtil = require('libraryUtil') local checkType = libraryUtil.checkType local arguments = {} -- Generate four different tidyVal functions, so that we don't have to check the -- options every time we call it. local function tidyValDefault(key, val) if type(val) == 'string' then val = val:match('^%s*(.-)%s*$') if val == '' then return nil else return val end else return val end end local function tidyValTrimOnly(key, val) if type(val) == 'string' then return val:match('^%s*(.-)%s*$') else return val end end local function tidyValRemoveBlanksOnly(key, val) if type(val) == 'string' then if val:find('%S') then return val else return nil end else return val end end local function tidyValNoChange(key, val) return val end local function matchesTitle(given, title) local tp = type( given ) return (tp == 'string' or tp == 'number') and mw.title.new( given ).prefixedText == title end local translate_mt = { __index = function(t, k) return k end } function arguments.getArgs(frame, options) checkType('getArgs', 1, frame, 'table', true) checkType('getArgs', 2, options, 'table', true) frame = frame or {} options = options or {} --[[ -- Set up argument translation. --]] options.translate = options.translate or {} if getmetatable(options.translate) == nil then setmetatable(options.translate, translate_mt) end if options.backtranslate == nil then options.backtranslate = {} for k,v in pairs(options.translate) do options.backtranslate[v] = k end end if options.backtranslate and getmetatable(options.backtranslate) == nil then setmetatable(options.backtranslate, { __index = function(t, k) if options.translate[k] ~= k then return nil else return k end end }) end --[[ -- Get the argument tables. If we were passed a valid frame object, get the -- frame arguments (fargs) and the parent frame arguments (pargs), depending -- on the options set and on the parent frame's availability. If we weren't -- passed a valid frame object, we are being called from another Lua module -- or from the debug console, so assume that we were passed a table of args -- directly, and assign it to a new variable (luaArgs). --]] local fargs, pargs, luaArgs if type(frame.args) == 'table' and type(frame.getParent) == 'function' then if options.wrappers then --[[ -- The wrappers option makes Module:Arguments look up arguments in -- either the frame argument table or the parent argument table, but -- not both. This means that users can use either the #invoke syntax -- or a wrapper template without the loss of performance associated -- with looking arguments up in both the frame and the parent frame. -- Module:Arguments will look up arguments in the parent frame -- if it finds the parent frame's title in options.wrapper; -- otherwise it will look up arguments in the frame object passed -- to getArgs. --]] local parent = frame:getParent() if not parent then fargs = frame.args else local title = parent:getTitle():gsub('/sandbox$', '') local found = false if matchesTitle(options.wrappers, title) then found = true elseif type(options.wrappers) == 'table' then for _,v in pairs(options.wrappers) do if matchesTitle(v, title) then found = true break end end end -- We test for false specifically here so that nil (the default) acts like true. if found or options.frameOnly == false then pargs = parent.args end if not found or options.parentOnly == false then fargs = frame.args end end else -- options.wrapper isn't set, so check the other options. if not options.parentOnly then fargs = frame.args end if not options.frameOnly then local parent = frame:getParent() pargs = parent and parent.args or nil end end if options.parentFirst then fargs, pargs = pargs, fargs end else luaArgs = frame end -- Set the order of precedence of the argument tables. If the variables are -- nil, nothing will be added to the table, which is how we avoid clashes -- between the frame/parent args and the Lua args. local argTables = {fargs} argTables[#argTables + 1] = pargs argTables[#argTables + 1] = luaArgs --[[ -- Generate the tidyVal function. If it has been specified by the user, we -- use that; if not, we choose one of four functions depending on the -- options chosen. This is so that we don't have to call the options table -- every time the function is called. --]] local tidyVal = options.valueFunc if tidyVal then if type(tidyVal) ~= 'function' then error( "bad value assigned to option 'valueFunc'" .. '(function expected, got ' .. type(tidyVal) .. ')', 2 ) end elseif options.trim ~= false then if options.removeBlanks ~= false then tidyVal = tidyValDefault else tidyVal = tidyValTrimOnly end else if options.removeBlanks ~= false then tidyVal = tidyValRemoveBlanksOnly else tidyVal = tidyValNoChange end end --[[ -- Set up the args, metaArgs and nilArgs tables. args will be the one -- accessed from functions, and metaArgs will hold the actual arguments. Nil -- arguments are memoized in nilArgs, and the metatable connects all of them -- together. --]] local args, metaArgs, nilArgs, metatable = {}, {}, {}, {} setmetatable(args, metatable) local function mergeArgs(tables) --[[ -- Accepts multiple tables as input and merges their keys and values -- into one table. If a value is already present it is not overwritten; -- tables listed earlier have precedence. We are also memoizing nil -- values, which can be overwritten if they are 's' (soft). --]] for _, t in ipairs(tables) do for key, val in pairs(t) do if metaArgs[key] == nil and nilArgs[key] ~= 'h' then local tidiedVal = tidyVal(key, val) if tidiedVal == nil then nilArgs[key] = 's' else metaArgs[key] = tidiedVal end end end end end --[[ -- Define metatable behaviour. Arguments are memoized in the metaArgs table, -- and are only fetched from the argument tables once. Fetching arguments -- from the argument tables is the most resource-intensive step in this -- module, so we try and avoid it where possible. For this reason, nil -- arguments are also memoized, in the nilArgs table. Also, we keep a record -- in the metatable of when pairs and ipairs have been called, so we do not -- run pairs and ipairs on the argument tables more than once. We also do -- not run ipairs on fargs and pargs if pairs has already been run, as all -- the arguments will already have been copied over. --]] metatable.__index = function (t, key) --[[ -- Fetches an argument when the args table is indexed. First we check -- to see if the value is memoized, and if not we try and fetch it from -- the argument tables. When we check memoization, we need to check -- metaArgs before nilArgs, as both can be non-nil at the same time. -- If the argument is not present in metaArgs, we also check whether -- pairs has been run yet. If pairs has already been run, we return nil. -- This is because all the arguments will have already been copied into -- metaArgs by the mergeArgs function, meaning that any other arguments -- must be nil. --]] if type(key) == 'string' then key = options.translate[key] end local val = metaArgs[key] if val ~= nil then return val elseif metatable.donePairs or nilArgs[key] then return nil end for _, argTable in ipairs(argTables) do local argTableVal = tidyVal(key, argTable[key]) if argTableVal ~= nil then metaArgs[key] = argTableVal return argTableVal end end nilArgs[key] = 'h' return nil end metatable.__newindex = function (t, key, val) -- This function is called when a module tries to add a new value to the -- args table, or tries to change an existing value. if type(key) == 'string' then key = options.translate[key] end if options.readOnly then error( 'could not write to argument table key "' .. tostring(key) .. '"; the table is read-only', 2 ) elseif options.noOverwrite and args[key] ~= nil then error( 'could not write to argument table key "' .. tostring(key) .. '"; overwriting existing arguments is not permitted', 2 ) elseif val == nil then --[[ -- If the argument is to be overwritten with nil, we need to erase -- the value in metaArgs, so that __index, __pairs and __ipairs do -- not use a previous existing value, if present; and we also need -- to memoize the nil in nilArgs, so that the value isn't looked -- up in the argument tables if it is accessed again. --]] metaArgs[key] = nil nilArgs[key] = 'h' else metaArgs[key] = val end end local function translatenext(invariant) local k, v = next(invariant.t, invariant.k) invariant.k = k if k == nil then return nil elseif type(k) ~= 'string' or not options.backtranslate then return k, v else local backtranslate = options.backtranslate[k] if backtranslate == nil then -- Skip this one. This is a tail call, so this won't cause stack overflow return translatenext(invariant) else return backtranslate, v end end end metatable.__pairs = function () -- Called when pairs is run on the args table. if not metatable.donePairs then mergeArgs(argTables) metatable.donePairs = true end return translatenext, { t = metaArgs } end local function inext(t, i) -- This uses our __index metamethod local v = t[i + 1] if v ~= nil then return i + 1, v end end metatable.__ipairs = function (t) -- Called when ipairs is run on the args table. return inext, t, 0 end return args end return arguments

Different to Obsidian, Ayanad is RNG based on stats, given that it is sealed and gives one of the pieces types randomly. The different states Illustrious Illustrious is the first step towards Ayanad and is crafted with no previous gear piece. Epherium Epherium is the third step towards Ayanad and requires a certain piece of Magnificent gear to be crafted. Delphinad Delphinad is the forelast step towards Ayanad and requires a certain piece of Epherium gear to be crafted. Ayanad Ayanad is the last step and requires a certain piece of Delphinad gear to be crafted. The Guild Cloak, also commonly referred to as a Prestige Cloak, is a piece of Equipment that can be purchased from the Prestige Shop using Prestige or by completing the first section (Grand) of the Adventurer's Guide. Guild Cloaks are one of the most accessible pieces of equipment available to players. They can be obtained relatively early and upgraded over time through Synthesis. Obtaining a Guild Cloak Upon completing the first set of tasks in the Adventurer's Guide you will receive a box that contains a Guild Cloak, be sure to select which one you want carefully! To obtain more Guild Cloaks, the player must first be a member of a Guild. Players earn Prestige by completing Guild Missions and certain quests. Once 150 Prestige has been accumulated, a Guild Cloak can be purchased from the Prestige Shop. Choosing a Cloak Several different Guild Cloaks are available. Each cloak provides a different effect, allowing players to choose one that complements their class and playstyle. Once upgraded to Delphinad these cloaks branch out even further giving you 2 options of stats per cloak, I'll show these in the table as "Honor ver." and "Flaming ver.". Cloak Effect Honor ver. Flaming ver. Recommended for Twintail Cloak Block and Parry Rate Magic Defense Max Health Tank Arrowflash Cloak Attack Speed Backstab Melee Damage Melee Critical Damage Melee Windsong Cloak Move Speed Defense Penetration Ranged Critical Damage Archer Hatchetblade Cloak Cast Time Magic Defense Penetration Magic Critical Damage Mage Bastion Cloak Max Health Healing Power Critical Heal Bonus Healer Note: The recommended uses are general guidelines. Players should choose the cloak that best suits their class and build. Upgrading a Guild Cloak Guild Cloaks are upgraded using Synthesis. Synthesis increases the cloak's experience and allows it to advance through higher Grades. Synthesis Open your Inventory. Open the "Regrade Item" window. Select the Synthesis option. Place the Guild Cloak into the "Base Costume" slot. Add the required Synthesis Materials. Confirm the synthesis. Each synthesis grants experience to the cloak. Once enough experience has been accumulated, the cloak advances to the next grade. As the cloak's grade increases, its effects become more powerful. Synthesis Materials Guild Cloaks require specific Synthesis Materials to be upgraded. These materials can be obtained primarily through killing monsters in Diamond Shores after your faction has killed the Alemine Fortress which purifies the zone for a few days. You can also obtain cloak synthesis materials from killing monsters in other purified areas in Auroria called "Auroria Purification Zones" and you can find these in Sungold Fields, Exeloch, Calmlands, Marcala, Nuimari and Heedmar. Beware though as depending on who's faction purified the zone there will be a tower at the center of the area that will kill anyone not of the same faction. The materials required and the amount of Synthesis experience provided depend on the grade of the synthesis material. Synthesis Material Experience Different synthesis materials provide different amounts of Synthesis EXP when used to upgrade a cloak. The amount of EXP provided depends on the material's grade. Auroran Synthesis Shards are available in Basic, Grand and Rare grades, while Auroran Synthesis Stones are available in Arcane, Heroic and Unique grades. Auroran Synthesis Shard Grade Synthesis EXP Basic 75 Grand 112 Rare 168 Auroran Synthesis Stone Grade Synthesis EXP Arcane 252 Heroic 378 Unique 567 Experience Required The amount of EXP required to increase a cloak's grade varies depending on its tier. The table below shows both the EXP required for each individual grade increase and the total cumulative EXP required to reach that grade from the beginning of the respective tier. For example, an Epherium cloak requires 75 EXP to reach Grand, while reaching Divine requires 21,004 total EXP. Tiering it up In order to tier a cloak up to its next tier you need to have reached the max grade of your current tier, whether you reach 0% or 100% EXP at max grade does not have any impact on the next tier. Once that has been completed you just need some materials to tier your cloak up which will reset the stats it has, make the grade go back down to its lowest possible grade and reset the EXP. This means that until you reach Erenor cloak you don't have to be super min-maxxy with stats, just use the stats you are able to get on it. Tier Max Grade Epherium Divine Delphinad Epic Ayanad Legendary Erenor Mythic Rolling for different stats Upon grade up you are given a choice to either keep your stats as they are or to replace one of your current ones with a new random one. Important: Each grade increase provides one opportunity to replace one existing stat. If a single synthesis provides enough EXP to increase the cloak by multiple grades, only one of those grade-up rerolls is available. To maximize the number of reroll opportunities, avoid providing enough EXP to skip a grade. By pressing the magnifying glass you are able to see which stats are in the pool of the next grade when you are in the Synthesis tab. If you switch over to the Replace Effects tab you will see the stats that are in the pool of your current grade. DO NOT mix these two up when you are rolling for stats as that can lead to unwanted outcomes. Cryptic Lucky Scrolls can be used to replace a single stat on Ayanad or higher cloaks with a new random one from the stat pool. You can find the entire pool of stats you can get with the Cryptic Lucky Scroll by pressing the magnifying glass in the "Replace Effects" tab of the Synthesis window. It is recommended to ONLY use these on Erenor cloaks. Stats by Grade The stats available on a cloak are determined by its tier and grade. As a cloak is upgraded through its grades additional stats are introduced into the pool of possible stats that can be rolled. The table below shows when each group of stats is added to the rollable stat pool. Tier Grade Stats added to the pool Epherium Basic Main stat (Strength, Agility, Stamina, Spirit or Intelligence depending on cloak) Arcane The four remaining base stats (Strength, Agility, Stamina, Spirit, Intelligence) Delphinad Grand Main stat (Honor or Flaming version) Arcane Strength, Agility, Stamina, Spirit, Intelligence Ayanad Rare Main stat (Honor or Flaming version) Arcane Strength, Agility, Stamina, Spirit, Intelligence Divine Max Mana, Focus, Resilience, Received Healing, In-Battle Health Regen, Post-Cast Mana Regen, Fixed Melee Damage Reduction, Fixed Ranged Damage Reduction, Fixed Magic Damage Reduction Erenor Arcane Signature stat (Honor or Flaming version) Heroic Strength, Agility, Stamina, Spirit, Intelligence Celestial Max Mana, Focus, Resilience, Received Healing, In-Battle Health Regen, Post-Cast Mana Regen, Fixed Melee Damage Reduction, Fixed Ranged Damage Reduction, Fixed Magic Damage Reduction Number of Stat Slots As you upgrade a cloak through its grades, it gains additional stats. Epherium to Ayanad Cloaks: Start with 1 stat at the lowest grades and gradually gain up to 3 stats at the highest grade. Erenor Cloaks: Follow the same progression, but gain a 4th stat upon reaching Mythic grade. In other words the cloak's grade determines how many stats it has, with higher grades providing additional stats. Grade Epherium Delphinad Ayanad Erenor Basic – Arcane 1 1 1 1 Heroic – Celestial 2 2 2 2 Divine – Legendary 3 3 3 3 Mythic — — — 4 Changing to a different cloak Currently there is only one way to change your cloak into a different cloak and that is with an item called Ipnysh Cloakmuter. It can only be used on Erenor cloaks but lets you change your cloak to any of the other cloaks. This process resets the grade, stats and EXP of the cloak so you will have to get back on the Synthesis grind in order to make it Mythic again. Why Get a Guild Cloak? The Guild Cloak provides an accessible way for players to obtain significant amounts of useful stats through spending time grinding rather than spending a lot of gold and resources. Because the cloak can be upgraded through synthesis and tiered up multiple times, you can continue investing into the same item as your character progresses. Brave Warrior's Medals are a special event currency introduced during the 3rd Anniversary celebration. They are primarily used to guarantee the crafting of Halcyona Necklaces up to Rank 11. Brave Warrior's Medals are obtained by participating in several faction PvP events during the anniversary celebration, including Mistmerrow War, Golden Plains Battle, Veroe Harvest Festival, and Great Heist. Obtaining Brave Warrior's Medals can be obtained from the following events: Event Source Quest Mistmerrow War Point Rewards The Battle of Mistmerrow Basin Golden Plains Battle Victory Reward Obtained by interacting with the crystal Veroe Harvest Festival Victory Reward The Great Heist Kill Quest & Victory Rewards Capibaras and Their Tendency for Murder & Great Golden Getaway Note: Brave Warrior's Medals are an anniversary event currency and are only available from the designated anniversary event rewards. Usage It is recommended to only use this currency on Rank 11 as that will on average reduce the amount of Warrior's Medals you'll need for Rank 12 and beyond the most. Brave Warrior's Medals are used to guarantee the crafting of Halcyona Necklaces. They can be used to craft Unsealed Halcyona Necklaces up to Rank 11 (Epic), allowing players to bypass the normal randomness associated with obtaining a necklace of the desired rank. Item Purpose Brave Warrior's Medal Used to guarantee crafting a Rank 8–11 Halcyona Necklace

h: Tricking the Game Into Saving Your Settings
Settings Don't Save No Matter What
x: The Settings menu allows players to customize various aspects of ArcheAge Classic, including the user interface, graphics, controls, and gameplay options. Make sure you check out the "ArcheAge Classic" section in your Settings menu as there are plenty of custom settings for you to discover in there. Themes ArcheAge Classic offers three widely different UI themes which you can find at the bottom of your settings menu under "ArcheAge Classic" -> "Misc. Settings" -> "UI Customization". Classic - This is the regular light ArcheAge UI theme that we are all familiar with. ArcheWorld - This is a much darker theme, containing a lot of dark blues and blacks. This theme is available to everyone. Classic Dark (Premium) - This is your typical dark theme containing mostly shades of greys and blacks which are very easy on the eyes. To select this theme you need to have the Daru Blessing active. Themes Classic ArcheWorld Classic Dark (Premium) Name Colors If you navigate to Settings -> ArcheAge Classic -> Screen Options -> Nametag Color Settings you can change the colors of any of the names and HP bars you can see. These settings gives you a lot of freedom to alter the way you view other players and NPCs at a glance and can help you identify things much faster, for example if someone in your party/raid is Bloodlusted you can have their color set to a much more "friendly" color than what Bloodlusted players outside of your party/raid have. This lets you distinguish between friend and foe very easily. Example Player Name Colors Default White Yellow Dark Blue Ultra Mode ArcheAge Classic has custom Ultra graphics options that improves the look of the game immensely, they increase your view distance, increase your texture resolutions and more. The game looks very pretty with them turned on and don't result in a massive drop in framerate. The main issue comes with the increased amount of crashes these settings bring, therefore it is recommended to only use these settings when taking screenshots or making cinematic videos/clips. Tricking the Game Into Saving Your Settings After pressing "Exit Game" your settings are saved, just cancel the countdown. It is most commonly known that any settings you change during your current session will go lost if you were to crash. This is because the game doesn't properly save your settings until exitting the game. The point at which the game saves the settings is actually right after you press "Exit Game" so by cancelling the countdown you have effectively protected your new settings from being lost through a crash without actually closing the game. Troubleshooting New Install (Save Settings Crash Issue) If you just installed the game you want to make sure that you open the settings in Server Select or Character Select and press Apply before continuing. This is because if you were to try and start changing settings in-game without doing this at least once then the game will crash. UI Size Setting (Crashing Issue) The UI Size setting controls the size of the ArcheAge Classic user interface. This setting has been modified to allow for increasing your UI size to up to 160% which is quite "big" news for players using 4K monitors and the likes. There is one caveat to this setting after being modified and that is that you have to be in either Server Select of Character Select in order to change it. Any attempt in changing it in-game will result in a crash. Settings Don't Save No Matter What Some players may experience an issue where their settings revert to default values after restarting the game even if saving them properly. Possible Causes The game stores settings locally on the player's computer. If the game is unable to properly write to its configuration files, changes may not be saved. The most common fix to this issue is to navigate to C:\Users\YOUR USER\Documents\ and renaming the AAClassic folder found there to something like AAClassicOLD. The next time you start ArcheAge the AAClassic folder in your Documents folder will regenerate and in most cases this will fix your resetting settings issue. If however this did not fix your issue then you most likely have a program that interferes with the Documents folder, typically OneDrive is one such program that has a tendency of breaking the AAClassic folder within the Documents folder. This is because OneDrive specifically syncs everything in your Documents and likely impacts the game's ability to read/write within it. Turning off the Sync and/or OneDrive should fix the issue, you might need to regenerate the AAClassic folder like in the previous paragraph in order for it to start acting normal again.

The Dawnsdrop Pitchfork is an addition to the Dawnsdrop Tools custom content added in Patch 1.3.4. The Dawnsdrop Pitchfork is a Farming and Gathering tool that allows players to harvest crops and bundles into crates, which can later be opened for their materials. Higher-grade pitchforks provide increased yields when the crates are opened. Function The Dawnsdrop Pitchfork harvests a fully grown seed or bundle and converts it directly into a corresponding crate. Using the pitchfork does not consume Labor. Labor is instead consumed when opening the resulting crate. This allows players to harvest their crops without immediately spending Labor and save the crates for later. Higher-grade pitchforks also increase the amount of materials obtained when the crates are opened, making pitchforking more rewarding than conventional harvesting. There is however one downside to "Pitchforking" as it is known by, that is that you manually have to replant your farms unlike when you use the regular automated replanting option. This means you now have two distinct ways of managing Farming and Gathering: Active harvesting: Use the Pitchfork to harvest crops and bundles into crates. This provides increased yields but requires manually replanting crops. Passive/automated harvesting: Continue using the normal harvesting and automated replanting system. This requires less manual interaction but does not benefit from the Pitchfork's increased yields. Swirling Meadow is a brand new handcrafted (Crawling ♡) zone added in Patch 1.3.5h situated in southern Nuia (western continent). Swirling Meadow is a zone that primarily consists of New Player Housing areas, players with no ownership of any farms or buildings are capable of placing a single farm within this zone. Housing Areas Full map can be found on https://sermeatball.com/map Swirling Meadow was expanded in Patch February 5, 2026 which added a ton more space for farms, all of these under the New Player Housing rules. In order to place a farm in this zone you have to not own any other buildings elsewhere. These farms cannot be traded through regular means or have their taxes prepaid. Once you own a building elsewhere you will no longer be eligible to pay taxes on your Swirling Meadow farm, this means that you won't be receiving your weekly tax mail and your Swirling Meadow farm will be demolished within up to 2 weeks. Events The zone has been used to house multiple events so far, we've seen a race track with custom F1 vehicles, daily Capybara-themed quests and more. Swirling Meadow Race Event Kapiros Event

Taming is a custom proficiency that was added in Patch 1.3.6. Taming allows you to tame various beasts throughout the world of Erenor and use them as mounts. Increasing your Taming proficiency increases your effectiveness at taming beasts. Getting Started To begin Taming you are going to need to craft yourself the lowest tiered taming tool, the Greenhorn's Backpack. Recipe Greenhorn's Backpack Labor Cost × 150 Workbench Handicraft Kiln Materials Vita Seed × 5 Leather × 10 Apple × 10 Equip effect Taming skills enabled. Once you have crafted your backpack it is time to start searching for a group of beasts that all have the Beast of the Wild buff. This buff gives them a small chance to spawn a tameable version of themselves after dying. We have compiled a list of locations for all the tameables we were able to find down below. Taming is much like sport fishing, the beast will get a buff and you have to match that buff icon with one of the skills that your backpack provides when equipped. Taming skills: Wrestle the Wild - "Begin your attempt at taming a Wild beast." Soothe - "Calm the wild beast with words of comfort." NOTE: This skill is spammable and is your main way to get taming progress similar to the potency of Big Reel In from fishing. Feed - "Temper the beast's anger by feeding it." NOTE: This skill uses 1× Vita Root so be sure to bring many! Dance! - "Entertain the wild beast with a lively dance." Show of Strength - "Assert dominance over the beast! Dispels intimidated." NOTE: The tameable beast will every now and then cast intimidation on you and you have to dispel it using this skill. Wrangle - "Rein in the wild beast before it gets out of hand." Whistle of the Wild How to obtain In order to obtain the Whistle of the Wild you need to obtain a Mundane, Grand, Arcane or Celestial tamed beast and use a Wildcaller Flute to release the beast back to the wild and obtain an amount of Whistles depending on the Grade of the tamed beast. Warning! This removes the tamed beast in the process. Tamed Beast Average Mundane 1 Grand ~3 Arcane ~5 Celestial ~10 Uses Whistle of the Wild can be used for a plethora of custom Taming-related recipes. There are 2 backpack upgrades, 5 new mount consumables and 4 new mount armor sets with 3 tiers per set. h: Step 2.2 - Obtaining the Ayanad Starlight Blessing
x: Enlightened Ayanad Accessories are custom accessories that was added in Patch 1.3.6. Enlightened Ayanad Accessories allows you to improve on your Ayanad Accessories by changing their stats, adding a skill to your necklace or changing their effects into the whole new Library Accessory lineup. Enlightening an Ayanad Accessory Step 1 - Ayanad Accessory To begin the process you first need to obtain an Ayanad Accessory that you want to Enlighten. Do not worry about the main stats it gives, just consider which "Equip effect" you want. When enlightening it you'll be able to apply any stat combination onto them that you desire. This is just my opinion but considering this process is quite resource intensive I recommend at bare minimum to only enlighten Divine+ Ayanad Accessories. Use the in-game Equipment Encyclopedia to see each Enlightened version, their equip effects are slightly improved. Step 2 - Enlightened Runestone To enlighten an accessory you'll need to use an Enlightened Runestone on the Ayanad Accessory you have prepared. Recipe Enlightened Runestone Proficiency Handicrafts 50,000 Labor Cost × 200 Workbench Disciple's Workbench Materials Dormant Runestone × 1 Starlight Archeum Essence × 5 Ayanad Starlight Blessing × 1 Blue Salt Hammer × 50 Use: Spend 10 labor to unlock the secrets of Ayanad. Disciple's Workbench locations. Once crafted you will need to go to the top floor in Library to use the Enlightened Runestone on your accessory. The easiest way to achieve this is to buy a Ayanad Scroll: 3rd Floor Lobby from the Auction House to instantly teleport to the top of Library, it can be used from anywhere in Diamond Shores. Step 2.1 - Obtaining the Dormant Runestone The Dormant Runestone can rarely be obtained from Scholar's Research Bundle, Librarian's Research Bundle and Dean's Research Bundle which are obtained by killing monsters in Library. Step 2.2 - Obtaining the Ayanad Starlight Blessing Recipe Ayanad Starlight Blessing Proficiency N/A Labor Cost × 500 Workbench Ipnysh Altar Materials Acid Vessel × 2 Complete Cursed Armor × 2 Earthmana Leaf × 100 Prismatic Diamond × 25 Ayanad Accessory Scroll × 1 Black Pearl × 5 Acid Vessel × 1 requires Acid Goblet × 200 and 1,500 Labor. Acid Goblet can rarely be obtained when slaying monsters in Aegis Island. Complete Cursed Armor × 1 requires Cursed Armor Scrap × 200 and 1,500 Labor. Cursed Armor Scrap can rarely be obtained when slaying monsters in Whalesong Harbor. Step 3 - Lunasigils, Applying Stats Once an accessory is enlightened it loses its main stats. You can apply new stats on it using a Lunasigil. Example: You prepared an Ayanad Wave Earring for enlightenment. Before Runestone Earring Divine Ayanad Wave Earring Intelligence 25 Equip effect Decreases received damage -2.4%. After Runestone Earring Divine Enlightened Ayanad Wave Earring Equip effect Decreases received damage -2.8%. These are the Lunasigils you can craft and put into your Enlightened Accessories: Hybrid Stat Perfect Desert Lunasigil Strength 20 Stamina 20 Perfect Lake Lunasigil Stamina 20 Intelligence 20 Perfect Lightning Lunasigil Strength 20 Agility 20 Perfect Meadow Lunasigil Intelligence 20 Spirit 20 Perfect Meteor Lunasigil Strength 20 Spirit 20 Perfect Mist Lunasigil Agility 20 Spirit 20 Perfect Squall Lunasigil Agility 20 Stamina 20 Perfect Stone Lunasigil Stamina 20 Spirit 20 Perfect Sunset Lunasigil Strength 20 Intelligence 20 Perfect Tidal Lunasigil Agility 20 Intelligence 20 Pure Stat Perfect Earth Lunasigil Stamina 35 Perfect Flame Lunasigil Strength 35 Perfect Gale Lunasigil Agility 35 Perfect Life Lunasigil Spirit 35 Perfect Wave Lunasigil Intelligence 35 WARNING: Lunasigils cannot be stacked with the accessory Lunafrosts from the Loyalty Shop. We could for example apply a Perfect Earth Lunasigil onto our Enlightened Ayanad Wave Earring with this new feature resulting in a much stronger tank-oriented earring than the original Wave earrings. Row template for RecipeBox. One call per ingredient, filled in by External Data (#display_external_table). Parameters (named after the API fields): mid (the item ID, used to read the game's icon file name from aa-classic.com), material, grade (the item's own grade), required (the grade the recipe demands, "Any" if none), amount, mode. Coin rows (mode = currency) are skipped here. Coins are shown at the bottom by RecipeBox. The name colour and the icon border use the required grade when there is one, otherwise the item's own grade.

Template:RecipeBox Shows a craft recipe, fetched from the sermeatball crafting API. Workbench, proficiency and materials come from the API. Usage {{RecipeBox|9001323}} The only parameter is the craft ID. Needs the template RecipeMaterialLine.

Shows a craft recipe, fetched from the sermeatball crafting API. The recipe row shows how many items one craft makes. When the craft has a bonus rate above 100 (and below 1000, since 10000 is not a percentage), a "Chance for 2x" row shows the extra percentage. Workbench, proficiency and materials come from the API. Coins in the recipe are shown last in the Materials list. A Recipe Cost row shows the total price of the materials, and is left out when the API has no price for them. Both as Gold / Silver / Copper. Usage {{RecipeBox|9001323}} The craft ID is the only required parameter. The recipe is read from a data page stored on the wiki (Module:Data/Recipes/..., made by sync_wiki_data.py). Only the Recipe Cost is fetched live, it follows the market. A recipe that is not stored yet is read live from the API until the script has been run for it. After a recipe changes in the game, run the script with --recipe ID --refresh. float (optional): where the box sits on the page. right or left places it at that side with the text flowing around it, center centres it. Leave it out for a normal box in the flow of the page. Examples {{RecipeBox|9001323|float=right}} {{RecipeBox|9001323|float=left}} Needs the templates RecipeMaterialLine, Coins and Item, and the style page Template:RecipeBox/styles.css. On narrow screens (phones) a floated box gets its own line instead of squeezing the text. No description. Where the box sits on the page: right or left (text flows around it) or center. Leave empty for a normal box in the flow of the page. Suggested values right left center String optional

local p = {} -- Grade name -> number of the border image (File:Grade1.png ... File:Grade11.png) local GRADES = { Basic = 1, Grand = 2, Rare = 3, Arcane = 4, Heroic = 5, Unique = 6, Celestial = 7, Divine = 8, Epic = 9, Legendary = 10, Mythic = 11, } -- Characters the wiki does not accept in file names, and what is used instead. -- KEEP THIS IN SYNC with the REPLACE table in upload_icons.py local CHARS = { [':'] = '-', ['['] = '(', [']'] = ')', ['#'] = '-', ['<'] = '-', ['>'] = '-', ['|'] = '-', ['{'] = '(', ['}'] = ')', ['/'] = '-', ['\\'] = '-', -- game icons in a folder: "aac/taming_bag_t3.png" -> File:Aac-taming_bag_t3.png } local function fileName(s) return (mw.ustring.gsub(s, '.', function(c) return CHARS[c] end)) end -- Icon file name from the game data ("icon_item_3400.png", "icon_item_3400.dds", "aac/taming_bag_t3.png") -- -> the name of the file on the wiki. Empty when there is no file name. function p.iconFile(name) name = mw.text.trim(tostring(name or '')) if name == '' or name == 'null' then return '' end name = name:gsub('%.%w+$', '') .. '.png' return fileName(name) end -- Item name -> icon file name part function p.name(frame) return fileName(mw.text.trim(frame.args[1] or '')) end -- Icon with the grade border painted on top. -- {{#invoke:IconName|icon|Item name|Grade|size=32}} -- No grade, "Any", "None", "Crude" or unknown -> Basic border (Grade1.png). -- file=icon_item_3400.png (optional): the game's own icon file name for the item. It is used when given, -- otherwise the file named after the item (the older way). -- over=top_seal_06.png (optional): the game's overlay picture for the item ("over_icon_filename"), painted on the icon -- under the grade border (sealed items, unconfirmed items ...). -- No "does the file exist" check on purpose: such checks are "expensive function calls" and a page is only -- allowed about 100 of them, which a page with several cards soon passes. function p.icon(frame) local args = frame.args local name = mw.text.trim(args[1] or '') local grade = mw.text.trim(args[2] or '') local size = tonumber(args.size) or 32 local file = fileName(name) local own = p.iconFile(args.file) if own ~= '' then file = own:gsub('%.png$', '') end -- "epic" / "EPIC" -> "Epic" grade = grade:sub(1, 1):upper() .. grade:sub(2):lower() local box = mw.html.create('span') :css('position', 'relative') :css('display', 'inline-block') :css('width', size .. 'px') :css('height', size .. 'px') :css('line-height', '0') :css('vertical-align', 'middle') :wikitext('[[File:' .. file .. '.png|' .. size .. 'px|link=]]') local over = p.iconFile(args.over) if over ~= '' then box:tag('span') :css('position', 'absolute') :css('top', '0') :css('left', '0') :wikitext('[[File:' .. over .. '|' .. size .. 'px|link=]]') end -- No grade (empty, "None", "Any", "Crude" ...) gets the Basic border, like in the game local n = GRADES[grade] or 1 if n then box:tag('span') :css('position', 'absolute') :css('top', '0') :css('left', '0') :wikitext('[[File:Grade' .. n .. '.png|' .. size .. 'px|link=]]') end return tostring(box) end return p

Shows an in-game style tooltip for a mount, fetched from the sermeatball API. Hover over a skill name to read what it does. Usage {{Mount|9002335}} The only parameter is the item ID of the mount. The name, grade, description, skills (with effects) and move speed all come from the API. The icon is the game's own icon of the item (icon_item_NNNN.png, read from aa-classic.com); if that file is not on the wiki, the file named after the mount is used. speed (optional): replaces the move speed from the API, in m/s. float (optional): where the card sits on the page. right or left places it at that side with the text flowing around it, center centres it. Leave it out for a normal card in the flow of the page. Examples {{Mount|9002335|float=right}} {{Mount|9002317|speed=11.7|float=left}} The data is read from data pages stored on the wiki (Module:Data/Mounts/..., made by sync_wiki_data.py), so the cards load without asking the APIs. A mount that is not stored yet is read live (cooldown, casting time and mana from aa-classic.com, one request per skill) until the script has been run for it. Needs Module:Mount, Module:IconName, Template:Grade, Template:MountSkillRow and Template:Mount/styles.css. No description. Template parameters Parameter Description Type Status Item ID 1 The item ID of the mount, for example 9002335 Number required Base move speed speed Optional. Replaces the move speed from the API, in m/s, for example 11.7 String optional Position float Optional. Where the card sits on the page: right or left (text flows around it) or center. Leave empty for a normal card in the flow of the page. Suggested values right left center String optional

local p = {} local IconName = require('Module:IconName') local Store = require('Module:DataStore') -- data stored on the wiki by sync_wiki_data.py -- Skill icons straight from aa-classic.com (the exact game icon of each skill). -- MediaWiki only shows images from other sites when the wiki owner allows it -- ($wgAllowExternalImagesFrom). Set this to true once that works, see Template:Mount docs. local EXTERNAL_ICONS = false local ICON_BASE = 'https://aa-classic.com/game/icons/' local ROW, COL = '‖', '¦' -- separators used by Template:Mount to hand the skill list over -- Make text safe to put inside HTML / wikitext local function esc(s) return mw.text.encode(tostring(s or ''), '<>&"'%[%]{}|') end local function trim(s) return mw.text.trim(tostring(s or '')) end -- "10.0" -> "10" local function int(s) local n = tonumber(s) if n then return tostring(n) end s = trim(s) if s == 'null' then return '' end return s end -- Remove colour codes we do not use local function clean(s) return (s:gsub('|c%x%x%x%x%x%x%x%x', ''):gsub('|r', '')) end -- Text outside colour codes. The game also highlights durations it fills in itself, which the data -- writes as "10s" (written-out times such as "3 seconds" are not highlighted). Shown as "10sec". local function plain(s) s = clean(s) local out, pos = {}, 1 while true do local a, b, num, unit = s:find('(%d[%d%.]*)([sm])%f[%A]', pos) if not a then break end local before = a > 1 and s:sub(a - 1, a - 1) or '' local isTime = (unit == 's') or (unit == 'm' and s:sub(math.max(1, a - 4), a - 1) == 'for ') if before:find('%w') or not isTime then out[#out + 1] = esc(s:sub(pos, b)) -- inside a word, or a distance like 25m: leave it else out[#out + 1] = esc(s:sub(pos, a - 1)) out[#out + 1] = '' .. esc(num) .. (unit == 's' and 'sec' or 'min') .. '' end pos = b + 1 end out[#out + 1] = esc(s:sub(pos)) return table.concat(out) end -- Effect text. The game marks the values it highlights as |cFFRRGGBB...|r, e.g. "|cFFFF9C27+80%|r". -- Only those parts get a colour. Unfilled placeholders such as #{avg_damage} become "(varies)". local NCODE = { c = 'FF9C27', i = 'F5CB65', d = 'A3E3FD' } -- |nc;| orange, |ni;| yellow, |nd;| light blue; other |n?; codes are dropped local function effectHtml(text) text = tostring(text or ''):gsub('#%b{}', '(varies)') text = text:gsub('|n(%a);(.-)|r', function(code, inner) if NCODE[code] then return '|cFF' .. NCODE[code] .. inner .. '|r' end return inner end) local out, pos = {}, 1 while true do local s, e, rgb, inner = text:find('|c%x%x(%x%x%x%x%x%x)(.-)|r', pos) if not s then break end out[#out + 1] = plain(text:sub(pos, s - 1)) out[#out + 1] = '' .. esc(clean(inner)) .. '' pos = e + 1 end out[#out + 1] = plain(text:sub(pos)) return (table.concat(out):gsub(' ', '
')) end -- The skills as sent by Template:Mount: -- "level¦name¦effect¦cooldown¦casting¦mana¦effect with colour codes¦icon file‖level¦name¦..." -- Result: ordered list of { level = "30", names = {...} } and a table name -> { effect, cooldown, casting, mana } local function parseSkillList(str) local groups, byLevel, info = {}, {}, {} for _, row in ipairs(mw.text.split(tostring(str or ''), ROW, true)) do local f = mw.text.split(row, COL, true) local name = trim(f[2]) if name ~= '' then local lv = int(f[1]) local g = (lv ~= '') and byLevel[lv] or nil -- skills without a level each get their own line if not g then g = { level = lv, names = {} } if lv ~= '' then byLevel[lv] = g end groups[#groups + 1] = g end g.names[#g.names + 1] = name local coloured = trim(f[7]) info[name] = { effect = coloured ~= '' and coloured or trim(f[3]), cooldown = trim(f[4]), casting = trim(f[5]), mana = trim(f[6]), icon = trim(f[8]) } end end return groups, info end -- "30s" -> "30sec" local function secs(s) return (s:gsub('(%d)s%f[%A]', '%1sec'):gsub('(%d)m%f[%A]', '%1min')) end -- Fallback: cut skills out of the plain description ("Lv30: Overwhelm or Drop Back"). -- Returns the intro lines and the skill groups (no effect texts). local function parseDescription(text) text = (tostring(text or ''):gsub(' ', '')) local starts = {} -- "Lv20: Name" and "Level 20: Name" (some mounts, e.g. the candy-fueled snails, write it out) for _, word in ipairs({ 'Lv', 'Level' }) do local init = 1 while true do local s, e, lv, colon = text:find(word .. '%s*(%d+)%s*(:?)', init) if not s then break end init = e + 1 -- the data sometimes forgets the colon ("Lv20 Name"), accepted at the start of a line local lineStart = (s == 1) or text:sub(s - 1, s - 1) == ' ' if colon == ':' or lineStart then starts[#starts + 1] = { s = s, e = e, lv = lv } end end end table.sort(starts, function(a, b) return a.s < b.s end) local intro, groups = text, {} if #starts > 0 then intro = text:sub(1, starts[1].s - 1) for i, st in ipairs(starts) do local stop = starts[i + 1] and (starts[i + 1].s - 1) or #text local spec = trim(text:sub(st.e + 1, stop)) local names = {} for _, n in ipairs(mw.text.split(spec, ' or ', true)) do n = trim(n) if n ~= '' then names[#names + 1] = n end end groups[#groups + 1] = { level = st.lv, names = names } end end local lines = {} for _, l in ipairs(mw.text.split(intro, ' ', true)) do l = trim(l) if l ~= '' then lines[#lines + 1] = l end end return lines, groups end -- One skill name with its hover box -- name: the skill's own name (title and icon of the hover box); shown: the text on the page if it differs local function skillNode(name, skills, shown) local info = skills[name] or {} local effect = info.effect if effect == '' then effect = nil end local s = mw.html.create('span'):addClass('aa-mskill'):attr('tabindex', '0') s:wikitext(esc(shown or name)) local tip = s:tag('span'):addClass('aa-mskill-tip') local head = tip:tag('span'):addClass('aa-mskill-head') local ext = info.icon or '' if EXTERNAL_ICONS and ext:match('^[%w_%-%.]+%.png$') then head:tag('span'):addClass('aa-mskill-icon'):wikitext(ICON_BASE .. ext) else -- the skill's own game icon (icon_skill_....png). No check that the file exists: such checks are -- "expensive function calls" (about 100 allowed per page). A skill without icon data gets no icon. local fname = IconName.iconFile(ext) if fname ~= '' then head:tag('span'):addClass('aa-mskill-icon'):wikitext('[[File:' .. fname .. '|40px|link=]]') end end head:tag('span'):addClass('aa-mskill-name'):wikitext(esc(name)) -- mana, casting time, cooldown (only when the skill data was found) local mana = tonumber(info.mana) or 0 local cd = info.cooldown or '' local cast = info.casting or '' if cd == 'null' then cd = '' end if cast == 'null' or cast == '0' or cast == '0s' then cast = '' end if cd ~= '' or cast ~= '' or mana > 0 or info.casting == '0s' then local box = tip:tag('span'):addClass('aa-mskill-meta') if mana > 0 then box:tag('span'):addClass('aa-mskill-metaline'):wikitext('Mana ' .. esc(int(info.mana))) end if cast == '' then box:tag('span'):addClass('aa-mskill-metaline'):wikitext('Instant') else box:tag('span'):addClass('aa-mskill-metaline'):wikitext('Cast Time ' .. esc(secs(cast))) end if cd ~= '' then box:tag('span'):addClass('aa-mskill-metaline'):wikitext(esc(secs(cd)) .. ' Cooldown') end end if effect then tip:tag('span'):addClass('aa-mskill-effect'):wikitext(effectHtml(effect)) else tip:tag('span'):addClass('aa-mskill-none'):wikitext('No description yet.') end return s end -- One hoverable skill name, used by Module:Glider (through Template:GliderSkill). -- Args: name (the text on the page), realname (the skill's own name from its data: title and icon of the -- hover box, optional), color (RRGGBB, optional), cd, cast, mana, desc (with colour codes), icon function p.hover(frame) local a = frame.args local shown = trim(a.name) local name = trim(a.realname) if name == '' or name == 'null' then name = shown end local skills = { [name] = { effect = trim(a.desc), cooldown = trim(a.cd), casting = trim(a.cast), mana = trim(a.mana), icon = trim(a.icon) } } local node = skillNode(name, skills, shown) local c = trim(a.color):match('^%x%x%x%x%x%x$') if c then node:attr('style', 'color:#' .. c .. '; border-bottom-color:#' .. c) end return tostring(node) end -- A failed API request (with "suppress error" in the template) leaves External Data's own error text -- behind. Treat that as "no data" instead of showing it. local function fetched(s) s = trim(s) if s:find('class="error"', 1, true) then return '' end return s end -- The skills of a stored mount in the same text form Template:Mount hands over for live data: -- "level¦name¦effect¦cooldown¦casting¦mana¦effect with colour codes¦icon‖..." local function storedSkillString(stored) local rows = {} for _, s in ipairs(stored.skills or {}) do local sk = Store.get('Skills', s.id) or {} rows[#rows + 1] = table.concat({ s.lv and tostring(s.lv) or '', s.name or '', s.desc or '', sk.cd or '', sk.cast or '', sk.mana and tostring(sk.mana) or '', sk.desc or '', sk.icon or '' }, COL) .. ROW end return table.concat(rows) end -- Template:Mount sends the ID (id=) when the data is stored on the wiki. Without it the live data of the -- API comes in the other arguments. function p.card(frame) local a = frame.args local stored = Store.get('Mounts', a.id) local name = stored and trim(stored.name) or fetched(a.name) if name == '' then return '' end local grade = stored and trim(stored.grade) or fetched(a.grade) local gradeKnown = grade ~= '' -- empty = the grade could not be fetched: no grade line if grade == '' or grade == 'None' or grade == 'Any' then grade = 'Basic' end -- mounts without a grade count as Basic local speed = fetched(a.speed) -- a speed written in the template replaces the stored one if speed == '' and stored and stored.speed then speed = tostring(stored.speed) end local float = trim(a.float):lower() -- optional: right / left / center if float ~= 'right' and float ~= 'left' and float ~= 'center' then float = '' end local desc = stored and trim(stored.desc) or fetched(a.desc) local skillStr if stored then skillStr = storedSkillString(stored) else skillStr = tostring(a.skills or '') -- read last: expanding it fetches the skill data if skillStr:find('class="error"', 1, true) then skillStr = '' end end local gcls = (grade:lower():gsub('[^%a]', '')) -- Colours come from Template:Grade, so there is one place to change them local function colored(g, text) return frame:expandTemplate{ title = 'Grade', args = { g, text } } end local icon = IconName.icon({ args = { name, grade, size = 48, file = stored and trim(stored.icon) or fetched(a.icon) } }) local root = mw.html.create('div'):addClass('aa-mount'):addClass('aa-mgrade-' .. gcls) if float ~= '' then root:addClass('aa-mount-' .. float) end -- header: icon, category, grade, name local head = root:tag('div'):addClass('aa-mount-head') head:tag('div'):addClass('aa-mount-icon'):wikitext(icon) local title = head:tag('div'):addClass('aa-mount-title') title:tag('div'):addClass('aa-mount-cat'):wikitext('[[Mounts|Mount]]') if gradeKnown then title:tag('div'):addClass('aa-mount-grade'):wikitext(colored(grade, esc(grade))) end title:tag('div'):addClass('aa-mount-name'):wikitext(colored(grade, esc(name))) root:tag('div'):addClass('aa-mount-sep') -- description and skills local lines, fallbackGroups = parseDescription(desc) local groups, skills = parseSkillList(skillStr) if #groups == 0 then groups = fallbackGroups end -- Some skills have no unlock level in the data (e.g. "Ant's Diligence"), but the description -- says which level they belong to. Match them by name (ignoring case, punctuation and doubled -- letters, so the description's typo "Dilligence" still matches) and move them into that row. local function key(s) s = tostring(s):lower():gsub('%f[%a]the%f[%A]', '') -- "Launch the Owner" = "Launch Owner" s = s:gsub('[^%a%d]', '') return (s:gsub('(%a)%1', '%1')) -- doubled letters -> single end -- Skill names the description lists on a line of their own, before the first level ("Buck Up, Friends!") local introKeys = {} for _, l in ipairs(lines) do introKeys[key(l)] = true end -- sort position of a row: skills listed without a level come first, then by level, level-less ones last local function lvl(g) if g.keep then return -1 end return tonumber(g.level) or 1e9 end -- number of single-letter edits between two strings local function distance(a, b) local prev = {} for j = 0, #b do prev[j] = j end for i = 1, #a do local cur = { [0] = i } for j = 1, #b do local cost = (a:sub(i, i) == b:sub(j, j)) and 0 or 1 cur[j] = math.min(prev[j] + 1, cur[j - 1] + 1, prev[j - 1] + cost) end prev = cur end return prev[#b] end local descLevel, descOrder, descKeys, descGroup, descCount, descFirst = {}, {}, {}, {}, {}, {} for gi, dg in ipairs(fallbackGroups) do descCount[dg.level] = (descCount[dg.level] or 0) + 1 if not descFirst[dg.level] then descFirst[dg.level] = gi end for i, n in ipairs(dg.names) do local k = key(n) descLevel[k] = dg.level descOrder[k] = i descGroup[k] = gi descKeys[#descKeys + 1] = k end end -- exact match on the simplified name, otherwise the closest name that is at most 2 letters off -- (the description misspells some names, e.g. "Release Poision"). Returns the description's key. local function findKey(name) local k = key(name) if descLevel[k] then return k end local best, bestD = nil, 3 for _, dk in ipairs(descKeys) do local d = distance(k, dk) if d < bestD then best, bestD = dk, d end end return best end -- Several skills of one level are "A or B" (a choice) only when the description writes them on one -- line. When it lists the same level on several lines ("Lv20: A" / "Lv20: B", like Carrot Dash), -- the mount gets all of them, so every description line becomes its own line here too. local split = {} for _, g in ipairs(groups) do if g.level ~= '' and (descCount[g.level] or 0) > 1 then local parts, order = {}, {} for _, n in ipairs(g.names) do local dk = findKey(n) local gi = dk and descGroup[dk] or descFirst[g.level] if not parts[gi] then parts[gi] = {}; order[#order + 1] = gi end parts[gi][#parts[gi] + 1] = n end table.sort(order) for _, gi in ipairs(order) do split[#split + 1] = { level = g.level, names = parts[gi], dg = gi } end else g.dg = descFirst[g.level] split[#split + 1] = g end end groups = split local merged, byDG = {}, {} for _, g in ipairs(groups) do if g.level ~= '' then if g.dg then byDG[g.dg] = g end merged[#merged + 1] = g end end local placed = false for _, g in ipairs(groups) do if g.level == '' then for _, n in ipairs(g.names) do local dk = findKey(n) local gi = dk and descGroup[dk] local target = gi and byDG[gi] if target then target.names[#target.names + 1] = n descOrder[key(n)] = descOrder[dk] placed = true elseif gi then -- the description has a line of its own for this skill (e.g. "Lv20 Powerful Wingbeats") local ng = { level = fallbackGroups[gi].level, names = { n }, dg = gi } byDG[gi] = ng merged[#merged + 1] = ng placed = true elseif #fallbackGroups > 0 and introKeys[key(n)] then -- listed in the description without a level: keep it, as the first row merged[#merged + 1] = { level = '', names = { n }, keep = true } placed = true else merged[#merged + 1] = { level = '', names = { n } } end end end end if placed then for _, g in ipairs(merged) do table.sort(g.names, function(a, b) return (descOrder[key(a)] or 99) < (descOrder[key(b)] or 99) end) end -- keep the rows in level order (same level: description order), level-less ones last for i, g in ipairs(merged) do g.idx = i end table.sort(merged, function(a, b) local la, lb = lvl(a), lvl(b) if la ~= lb then return la < lb end if (a.dg or 99) ~= (b.dg or 99) then return (a.dg or 99) < (b.dg or 99) end return a.idx < b.idx end) groups = merged end -- The description lists the mount's skills by level (like the game's tooltip). Then show them in that -- order (the API's order is arbitrary) and leave out skills that are on no level and not in the -- description (basic skills such as "Mounted Attack", which the game does not list either). if #fallbackGroups > 0 then local kept = {} for _, g in ipairs(groups) do if g.level ~= '' or g.keep then kept[#kept + 1] = g end end if #kept > 0 then for i, g in ipairs(kept) do g.idx = i end table.sort(kept, function(a, b) local la, lb = lvl(a), lvl(b) if la ~= lb then return la < lb end if (a.dg or 99) ~= (b.dg or 99) then return (a.dg or 99) < (b.dg or 99) end return a.idx < b.idx end) groups = kept end end local isSkill = {} for _, g in ipairs(groups) do for _, n in ipairs(g.names) do isSkill[key(n)] = true end end -- The API breaks long descriptions into short lines in the middle of sentences. Glue a line onto -- the previous one unless that one ended a sentence (. ! ? : or a closing quote). local paras = {} for _, l in ipairs(lines) do if not isSkill[key(l)] then -- the description may list the skill names again, we show them below local last = paras[#paras] if last and not last:find('[%.!%?:"'%)]$') then paras[#paras] = last .. ' ' .. l else paras[#paras + 1] = l end end end for _, para in ipairs(paras) do root:tag('div'):addClass('aa-mount-desc'):wikitext(esc(para)) end for _, g in ipairs(groups) do local line = root:tag('div'):addClass('aa-mount-skill') if g.level ~= '' then line:tag('span'):addClass('aa-mount-lv'):wikitext('Lv' .. esc(g.level)) line:wikitext(': ') end for i, n in ipairs(g.names) do if i > 1 then line:tag('span'):addClass('aa-mount-or'):wikitext(' or ') end line:node(skillNode(n, skills)) end end -- use, speed root:tag('div'):addClass('aa-mount-use'):wikitext('Use:') root:tag('div'):addClass('aa-mount-usetext'):wikitext('Summons a mount.') if speed ~= '' then local line = root:tag('div'):addClass('aa-mount-speed') line:wikitext('Base Move Speed ') line:tag('span'):addClass('aa-mount-speedval'):wikitext(esc(speed) .. 'm/s') end return tostring(root) end return p
